messages:
alejandra: Heads-up: I ran a quick keyboard-only walkthrough of the onboarding checklist and found a few accessibility friction points. Wanted to surface them before we lock visuals.

miles: +1 please share specifics.

harper: Thanks for doing that! Which checklist step was worst?

alejandra: The 'Sample projects' step. Observations: 1) the step toggle is after the whole list visually, but keyboard focus lands on the first card — so keyboard users have to tab through many cards to opt-in. 2) the sample card CTAs are links styled as divs and require two tab stops to trigger (bad). 3) the "Skip tour" control is low-contrast and placed in the top-right of the hero, which is easily missed by low-vision users.

ravi: Good catches. Proposals?

alejandra: Quick proposals: A) Move the opt-in toggle ("Show my projects / Connect repos") to before the list so it receives early focus. B) Make CTAs actual <button> elements with visible focus states. C) Move "Skip tour" into the header row as a real button and add visually-hidden explanatory text: "Skip onboarding tour — you can access it later from Help." D) Increase contrast for skip link to meet AA (4.5:1) and add an underline style on focus.

miles: Agree A+B. For C, product asked UX to keep Skip less prominent to preserve guidance completion rates. Could we compromise by making Skip a secondary button (normal contrast but distinct) and add an explicit keyboard shortcut (e.g., pressing 'k' when focused on checklist) announced via tooltip / aria-describedby?

harper: Keyboard shortcut is neat but discoverability is a concern. Screen reader users won't know about it unless we surface it. We could show a small "Keyboard: K" hint near the header that is visible but low-contrast (but still meets contrast). Also document it in the onboarding accessibility help.

a11y-bot: note: any global keyboard shortcut must be optional and documented; ensure it doesn't conflict with common assistive tech shortcuts. Run through NVDA/VoiceOver consonance tests.

ravi: About making CTAs buttons: we'll need dev signoff — buttons change event handlers. But makes sense for semantics and reduces tab stops.

miles: Implementation detail: replace anchor-like divs with <button class="sample-cta">Run demo</button>, keep same styling, and add tabindex=0 to card container so arrow keys can navigate cards if we implement arrow nav. Also expose aria-roledescription="sample card" and aria-label with name+lang.

alejandra: For aria-label examples: use 'Sample project: Docs Q&A (Python)'. Avoid exposing repo slugs verbatim; sanitize names if we surface user repos.

miles: Noted. Also add an aria-live region to announce when a step auto-completes: e.g., 'Sample demo completed' so screen reader users know the change.

harper: Contrast specifics: Skip button BG in dark theme currently #2B2B2B against #FFFFFF text gives 3.2:1. Need at least 4.5:1. Proposal: make Skip text #FFFFFF on #1F2937 or use an outline style with darker focus ring.


a11y-bot: accessibility checklist generated: ["toggle-before-list","ctas-as-buttons","skip-button-contrast","aria-live-on-complete","keyboard-shortcut-doc","nvda-voiceover-tests"]. Please add tickets.

ravi: I'll make tickets. Which one is highest priority?

alejandra: Toggle placement and CTAs -> high. Skip contrast -> medium (but important). aria-live -> high. Keyboard shortcut -> low until we research conflicts.

pm-bot: poll created: https://poll.company/product/skip-ux (expires in 48h) — Please vote on whether Skip should be prominent (button) vs secondary link vs keyboard-only (A/B/C).

miles: Quick wording tweak for the skip tooltip: current 'You can access onboarding later' -> change to 'You can access onboarding later from Help > Onboarding' (makes path explicit).

harper: Also add a micro-copy line under the toggle: 'Private: we only read repo names, not contents' when opting into showing user projects.

alejandra: Dev notes for backend: if user opts to show repos, sanitize display names, cap to 8 items, and do not cache beyond 12 hours by default (privacy). Also log only presence of opt-in (boolean) for analytics, not repo names.

ravi: I'll add those constraints in the ticket. Anyone object to 8 limit?

miles: 8 is fine. On smaller screens we'll show 1-3 and provide 'More' drawer.

harper: final ask: before launch, run a 5-person keyboard+screenreader test pass (NVDA + VoiceOver + mac VoiceOver quick check) and capture any regressions. I'll lead that.

alejandra: Thanks Harper. Action items in summary: 1) Miles - implement semantics changes (buttons + tabindex + aria labels) 2) Ravi - create tickets for prioritised fixes + backend privacy rules 3) Harper - run SR/KB test pass and produce short report 4) PM-bot - include poll result in onboarding epic.

miles: I'll start a PR with the button swaps and focus order changes today.

harper: I'll schedule the usability sessions and ping here with times.

alejandra: Great work team, let's keep the checklist keyboard-first. :white_check_mark:
